q: Which type of testing verifies that the software functions as intended and meets requirements?
explanation: Functional testing checks each component and feature to confirm it works correctly. Usability testing looks at how easy the interface is, not whether features work.

q: Which type of testing observes users interacting with the software, usually in a controlled space with moderators, to assess how easy and intuitive the interface is?
explanation: Usability testing lets users try the initial system while moderators watch, gathering feedback and spotting confusion. Accessibility testing focuses specifically on users with disabilities.

q: Which type of testing evaluates how the software behaves under various conditions, including load testing and stress testing?
explanation: Performance testing simulates many simultaneous users or high data volumes to find bottlenecks and confirm responsiveness and stability.

q: Which type of testing ensures the software is usable by people with disabilities and adheres to standards such as WCAG?
explanation: Accessibility testing checks compliance with standards like WCAG and uses assistive technologies, making the system inclusive for all users.

q: Which type of testing ensures that new changes, such as bug fixes or new features, do not negatively affect existing functionality?
explanation: Regression testing rechecks existing features after code is modified, through full or partial testing, and can reveal new bugs introduced by the change.

q: What is software refactoring?
options: Restructuring existing code without changing its external behavior
Adding new features based on user feedback
Testing the software under heavy load
Rewriting the software in a new programming language for a new platform
explanation: Refactoring tidies the internal code (readability, complexity, maintainability) while the program behaves the same for users. Adding features or porting to a new platform changes what it does or where it runs.

q: What is software maintenance?
options: The testing of software before its first release
The planning of a quality management system
The removal of duplicate code before deployment
The ongoing process of modifying and updating software after its initial release to correct faults, improve performance, or adapt to a changing environment
explanation: Maintenance happens after the initial release and keeps the software meeting user needs and technological advancements.

q: Which type of software maintenance fixes defects or bugs reported by users or discovered through testing, and is described as reactive?
explanation: Corrective maintenance responds to issues after they are raised. Preventive maintenance works before problems happen.

q: Which type of software maintenance updates the software to accommodate changes in the environment or technology, such as upgrades, hardware changes, or new technology standards?
explanation: Adaptive maintenance keeps the software working in a changed environment. Perfective enhances features from user feedback; preventive heads off future issues.

q: Which focuses on the processes used to produce the software, using systematic activities and audits to make sure those processes lead to high-quality outcomes?
explanation: Quality Assurance is process-focused. Quality Control is the actual testing and inspection of the product and is reactive.

q: Which approach seeks to improve quality in all aspects of an organization through continuous improvement and the involvement of all employees?
explanation: TQM is holistic: it covers the whole organization and every employee. Six Sigma is a data-driven method for reducing defects and variability.

q: Which methodology is data-driven, uses statistical tools, and focuses on reducing defects and variability in processes?
explanation: Six Sigma relies on statistics to reduce defects and variation. TQM is a broader culture of continuous improvement across the organization.

q: What is the failure rate of a process operating at six sigma?
explanation: A six sigma process fails only 0.00034% of the time, which is 3.4 defects per million opportunities, so it produces virtually no defects.

q: What does ISO 9001:2015 specify?
options: The guidelines for accessible web content
The requirements for a quality management system (QMS), focused on meeting customer expectations
The five phases of Six Sigma
explanation: ISO 9001:2015 is an international standard for a QMS. Certification shows effective processes and well-trained staff. Accessible web content is covered by WCAG.

q: Why is the methodology called Six Sigma?
options: It was created by six companies
Sigma is one standard deviation, and six such deviations should occur before the process results in a defect
It requires six employees per team
explanation: Sigma means one standard deviation in a data set. Six Sigma has five phases (DMAIC), not six.

q: Which reason for testing states that finding and fixing issues early is less costly than addressing them after deployment?
explanation: Cost-Effectiveness is about lower costs from early detection. Reduces Risk is about avoiding failures that cause user frustration or business losses.

q: Which list gives the key components of quality management?
options: Planning, assurance, control, improvement processes, and documentation
Define, measure, analyze, improve, and control
Functional, usability, performance, accessibility, and regression
explanation: Quality management involves planning, assurance, control, improvement processes, and documentation. The other lists are the DMAIC phases, maintenance types, and testing types.

q: Which is one of the three benefits of software refactoring?
options: It adds new features for users
It improves maintainability, because well-structured code is easier to modify and extend
It replaces the need for regression testing
It changes the external behavior of the program
explanation: The benefits are enhanced readability, reduced complexity, and improved maintainability. Refactoring never changes external behavior or adds features.

q: What is the correct order of the five phases of Six Sigma?
explanation: DMAIC: Define the problem, Measure it in numbers, Analyze the cause, Improve the process, then Control to maintain the solution.

q: In Six Sigma, which phase comes right after quantifying the problem in numbers and is used to discover the influencing variables?
explanation: Measure quantifies the problem; Analyze comes next and finds the cause. Improve then implements and verifies the solution.

q: In Six Sigma, which is the final phase, asking whether the goal is being met constantly?
explanation: Control comes last: it maintains the solution and controls the changes and environment. Improve comes just before it.

q: Which sequence correctly places testing and maintenance in the life of a software product?
options: Development and testing, deployment (initial release), then ongoing maintenance
explanation: Testing finds issues before deployment, when they are cheaper to fix. Maintenance is the ongoing work after the initial release.

q: Which is NOT one of the five types of testing in the lecture?
explanation: The five types are functional, usability, performance, accessibility, and regression. Refactoring is restructuring code, not a type of testing.

q: Which is NOT a common software refactoring technique?
options: Breaking down long methods into smaller tasks
Adding a new feature requested by users
explanation: The techniques are renaming, breaking down long methods, removing duplicate code, introducing design patterns, and simplifying conditions. A new feature changes behavior, so it is not refactoring.

q: Which maintenance type and description is mismatched?
options: Adaptive: fixing defects or bugs reported by users or found in testing
Corrective: reactive, responding to issues raised by users
Perfective: enhancing features or performance based on user feedback
Preventive: refactoring code, optimizing performance, or updating documentation to prevent future issues
explanation: Fixing reported bugs is corrective maintenance. Adaptive maintenance updates the software for changes in the environment or technology, such as upgrades or new hardware.

q: Which is NOT one of the 8 primary elements of TQM?
explanation: TQM requires decisions based on data rather than intuition or assumptions. The other elements include customer focus, process-centered, continuous improvement, leadership commitment, and communications.

q: Which is NOT one of the challenges of software maintenance in the lecture?
explanation: Regulatory compliance is a reason maintenance is important. The four challenges are complexity of existing code, evolving requirements, resource allocation, and technical debt.

q: After many users asked for it in reviews, a team adds a dark mode and speeds up the search feature of their app. Which type of maintenance is this?
explanation: Enhancing features or performance based on user feedback is perfective. Nothing was broken (not corrective) and the environment did not change (not adaptive).

q: Before enrollment week, a university simulates 10,000 students logging in at once to see if the portal slows down or crashes. Which type of testing is this?
explanation: Simulating many simultaneous users to find bottlenecks is performance (load and stress) testing.

q: After developers change the login page, testers recheck the checkout and profile pages, which were not touched, to make sure they still work. Which type of testing is this?
explanation: Rechecking unchanged features after a code change is regression testing. Here it is a full test, since parts that were not changed are checked too.
